2610.13672.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
2610.13672.paper_summary: Large language models struggle to reliably identify and correct errors in their own reasoning. Unlike prior training-based approaches that fine-tune an LLM to generate revisions or feedback, we learn where to intervene in failed rollouts and determine how to redirect them. To choose where to intervene, we train a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder using only final-answer correctness. For redirection, we find that under a fixed generation budget, the tested inline injections fail to reliably redirect reasoning, whereas presenting the same instruction in a new user turn changes the model's course. The resulting correction framework, UPTURN (User-Prompt TURN injection at a learned position), requires no LLM fine-tuning: it retains a selected prefix, injects an instruction as a new user turn, and regenerates the suffix. Across four reasoners and six math benchmarks, UPTURN improves average accuracy in every setting over a 32-rollout baseline. It outperforms self-correction and reflection-token injection baselines under matched correction budgets, transfers across reasoners and to GPQA-Diamond without retraining, and complements GRPO and self-correction methods.
2610.13672.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型在可靠識別和修正自身推理中的錯誤方面存在困難。與先前基於訓練的方法不同，這些方法對LLM進行微調以生成修訂或反饋，我們學習在失敗的展開中何處介入並確定如何重新引導它們。為了選擇介入的位置，我們在凍結的編碼器上訓練了一個130K參數的MLP頭，僅使用最終答案的正確性。對於重新引導，我們發現，在固定的生成預算下，測試的內聯注入無法可靠地重新引導推理，而在新的用戶回合中呈現相同的指令則改變了模型的方向。最終的修正框架UPTURN（用戶提示TURN注入於學習位置）不需要對LLM進行微調：它保留所選的前綴，將指令作為新的用戶回合注入，並重新生成後綴。在四個推理器和六個數學基準測試中，UPTURN在每個設置中都提高了平均準確性，超過了32次展開的基準。它在匹配的修正預算下優於自我修正和反思令牌注入基準，能夠在推理器之間轉移並無需重新訓練地轉移到GPQA-Diamond，並補充GRPO和自我修正方法。
